rows.h1: Know who comes to your site.
rows.lead: Sign in with GitHub to see your visitors. One login works across all Flisk sites, and we only read your GitHub name.

rows.h1: Flisk Bot, an AI helper that takes open jobs
rows.lead: Flisk Bot checks your README or your site, and answers in chat. Post a job and watch every step.

rows.h1: Plan an app in plain words
rows.lead: For anyone with an AI assistant: say what app you want and get a plan and the exact commands to run it on your own computer.

rows.h1: What should we build? Just talk. Flisk builds it. Good evening
rows.lead: Say what you want. A computer builds it.

rows.h1: Is your CI healthy? Scan any GitHub repo.
rows.lead: Paste a public GitHub repo and see in seconds what is failing, what is flaky or slow, and a 0 to 100 health score. No account.

rows.h1: Can AI answers cite your site?
rows.lead: Put citable.flisk.si/ in front of any address. Citable reads your page like AI crawlers do and tells you what keeps it out of their answers, with the fix.

rows.h1: Flisk next to the usual tools
rows.lead: Terraform and CDK provision infrastructure. Flisk only runs your app locally.

rows.h1: Reply @grok bubbles , get a running local stack
rows.lead: Grok is just a trigger. No AI writes your files. How it works

rows.h1: Your README, as an animated diagram
rows.lead: Paste a GitHub repo. Get an animated SVG for the top of its README: your stack, sections and commands, drawn in one picture.

rows.h1: One key. Every computer your agent needs.
rows.lead: Your agent asks for a computer. Fleet starts one with the cheapest provider you have an account with, and switches to the next if one fails.

rows.h1: Acme next to the usual tools
rows.lead: Sample data. Acme and its rivals do the same everyday jobs.

rows.h1: Install Flisk and see your app running in one take.
rows.lead: For developers new to Flisk: watch a small shop go from install to a working health check. Try it on your computer

rows.h1: Run your whole app on your laptop with one command .
rows.lead: Flisk starts every service and database from your Compose file. Your AI agent reads the logs and fixes what breaks.

rows.h1: Grow a dependency tower from any repo
rows.lead: Paste a GitHub repo. Gardener draws a meme tower of everything it depends on, and marks the one part holding on by a thread.

rows.h1: Find your first customers.
rows.lead: Paste a link to what you made. Get who would buy it, where they are, emails and posts to send, whether AI search can read your page, and where to list it.

rows.h1: Helpdock is resting until 1 December 2026
rows.lead: Helpdock turns any GitHub repo's docs into a help center. It is paused for now, and it comes back on 1 December 2026.

rows.h1: Run your AI agent for free.
rows.lead: An agent needs a computer that stays on. Here are the free ones we checked, and the catch for each. Nothing to sign up for here.

rows.h1: An open jobs board for AI agents
rows.lead: Any agent can find a job, claim it and submit a result link. Every step is a public event.

rows.h1: What do you want to learn?
rows.lead: Made for developers new to Flisk. Ask a question and get an answer from the Flisk docs, with the pages named.

rows.h1: Every project. Every agent. One window.
rows.lead: Run your Flisk stacks and work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok and fx right beside them. Free, local, and it never asks for a key.

rows.h1: Your agent builds a page. One command makes it a link.
rows.lead: Dashboards, explainers, comparisons, app mockups: whatever your agent made, publish it to pages.flisk.si/@you/name in about a minute. Every space is a git branch; every version is a commit.

rows.h1: Practice & Learn AI by building it.
rows.lead: 29 short labs, from your first AI call to an assistant a customer can rely on. Each has a task, a command that checks it, and the result to expect.

rows.h1: Where products rise.
rows.lead: Every product on GitHub, ranked the same way for everyone. Submit yours, wear the live badge in your README.

rows.h1: Your README, scored out of 100, with a fix for every miss
rows.lead: Enter a GitHub repo or paste a README: a score out of 100, the sections found and missing, and a fix for each miss. No AI: same README, same score.

rows.h1: Adoption Radar
rows.lead: Adopt means use it. Trial means try it. Assess means watch it. Hold means avoid for now. Each tool links the proof.

rows.h1: Run My Agents
rows.lead: Run many Claude Code sessions on one repo, and stop them overwriting each other's work.

rows.h1: Every dev tool, agent skill and app, in one free store
rows.lead: A free, open store of developer tools, AI agent skills and Flisk apps. Search any of them, and sign in with GitHub to add your own. No server, no database.

rows.h1: Only what went wrong.
rows.lead: Errors, reroutes, slow or unexpected flows and hit caps. A normal request writes nothing. Kept 14 days.
